concerns.concern: The claimed bulk-boundary correspondence paradox is an artefact of a wrong surface Brillouin zone. The surface reciprocal lattice is exactly the projection of the bulk reciprocal lattice, so bulk states and Weyl points are automatically periodic in the surface zone and nothing needs resolving.
concerns.quote: the central conceptual claim (items 1–2) rests on an incorrect construction of the surface Brillouin zone. Once the SBZ is constructed correctly, the "paradox" does not arise.

concerns.concern: The authors' chosen basis Pb₁, Pb₂ spans only an index-3 sublattice. Their "theoretical SBZ" is therefore three times too large, and the experimentally observed "new SBZ" is simply the correct conventional SBZ, which the referee's own numerical estimate confirms.
concerns.quote: The "new SBZ whose period along k∥ is one third of the theoretical SBZ" is therefore just the correct SBZ. The "theoretical SBZ" (purple lines) is three times too large.

concerns.concern: The LCM criterion, the 2π/3 phase between nonequivalent surface cells, and the momentum-space moiré are artefacts of the basis choice and should be removed or recast.
concerns.quote: the "LCM criterion"; the "2π/3 phase between three nonequivalent surface unit cells"; the "momentum-space moiré."

concerns.concern: The claim that hybridization relaxes the equality between a surface loop's Chern number and the enclosed projected chirality contradicts an established theorem. It should be dropped or backed by a concrete model calculation.
concerns.quote: Hybridization cannot change this.

concerns.concern: Fermi arcs "from different bulk BZs" do not exist as separate objects, because a bulk reciprocal-vector translation gives the same state. The picture of arcs hybridizing into loops is therefore unfounded, yet the main-text conclusions rely on it.
concerns.quote: Translating by a bulk reciprocal vector does not produce a new arc; it produces the same state.

concerns.concern: The claims that exact spectral reconstruction needs infinitely many projected BZs and that no finite cutoff captures all projected Weyl points are incorrect. One period along the normal, and the first BZ alone, suffice.
concerns.quote: The claims that "exact spectral reconstruction is achieved only in the infinite-projection limit" and that "no finite cutoff can fully capture all projected Weyl points" are incorrect.

concerns.concern: Irrational coefficients and N_min = ∞ cannot occur for any facet with integer Miller indices. N_min is just the sublattice index (|l|), so it is not a new criterion.
concerns.quote: N_min is simply the index of the sublattice spanned by Pb₁ and Pb₂, which equals |l| for a primitive basis and coprime indices. It is not a new criterion.

concerns.concern: The closed form a₁ = −h/l, a₂ = −k/l is said to hold only for orthogonal lattices, but it holds for every lattice and metric.
concerns.quote: In fact it holds for *every* lattice and every metric.

concerns.concern: The M_min^(adj) = 2N_min argument is ill-posed because copies of the same bulk BZ carry identical information. This also undermines the quasicrystal analogy.
concerns.quote: It compares truncated sets of BZ copies, but copies of the same bulk BZ carry identical (gauge-periodic) information.

concerns.concern: The supplementary redefinitions rescale basis vectors (2SBZ′ etc.) in order to preserve the desired conclusion.
concerns.quote: rescale basis vectors in order to preserve a desired conclusion. This is a symptom of the same problem.

concerns.concern: The authors should construct the SBZ directly from the in-plane translation lattice of the (103) plane and overlay it on Figs. 1, 2 and 4. They should also fold the first-BZ Weyl points into it and show the result matches Fig. 4d.
concerns.quote: Construct the SBZ directly from the 2D lattice of translations parallel to the (103) plane, and overlay it on Figs. 1, 2 and 4.

concerns.concern: The statement that the SBZ is determined by the (103) cross section of half a primitive unit cell needs explanation, because an SBZ is defined by the in-plane translation lattice.
concerns.quote: An SBZ is defined by the in-plane translation lattice, not by a cross-section of a 3D cell.

concerns.concern: The surface Fermi arc loop identification is not demonstrated. No signed crossing counts or enclosed projected chiralities are shown for loops L1–L4, and the authors should provide and compare these.
concerns.quote: No signed crossing count is shown, and no enclosed projected chirality is tabulated.

concerns.concern: A closed surface contour enclosing zero net chirality is just a topologically trivial surface state. It is not a new boundary topology inaccessible on high-symmetry facets.
concerns.quote: A closed surface contour that encloses zero net chirality is simply a topologically trivial surface state. Such states are common

concerns.concern: The abstract overstates the evidence for surface Fermi arc loops, even though the main text concedes they are unproven.
concerns.quote: the abstract ("experimental results further suggest…") overstates the evidence.

concerns.concern: The energies of the relevant Weyl points relative to E_F in the paramagnetic phase should be stated, together with a justification for looking for arcs at E_F.
concerns.quote: Please state where the relevant Weyl points (W1/W2/W3 families) lie relative to E_F in the paramagnetic phase.

concerns.concern: The surface preparation is not shown to give a flat, ordered (103) surface. XRD only confirms bulk orientation, so LEED and/or STM/AFM, the miscut angle, and the size of flat vs. uneven regions relative to the beam spot are needed.
concerns.quote: XRD (Fig. 1d) confirms the bulk orientation of the cut. It says nothing about surface flatness, faceting, or termination.

concerns.concern: Microfaceting into low-index terraces must be explicitly ruled out, since it could mimic or distort the observed periodicities.
concerns.quote: Microfaceting into low-index terraces such as (001) or (101) must be ruled out explicitly.

concerns.concern: The explanation of slab vs. Green's function differences is inaccurate. A correctly built slab has the same periodicity, and the poor six-layer result is due to thinness, not facet symmetry.
concerns.quote: A **six-layer** slab gives poor agreement because it is very thin.

concerns.concern: The slab comparison is unbalanced (36 layers for (001), 6 for (103)). A thickness-convergence test for the (103) slab is needed.
concerns.quote: the authors should show convergence of the (103) slab with thickness, for example 6, 20 and 40 layers.

concerns.concern: The disorder ordering is physically unexplained. Strong disorder should increase k⊥ broadening, yet it supposedly reveals k⊥-dispersive bulk states, so the uneven regions may differ in some other way.
concerns.quote: Physically, increasing disorder should shorten coherence and *increase* k⊥ broadening. The authors need a mechanism

concerns.concern: The disorder-filter selection logic is circular, because surface resonances should also be suppressed by disorder. A quantitative criterion is needed to isolate them.
concerns.quote: "Disorder suppresses surface weight" therefore cannot by itself isolate SBRSs. A quantitative criterion is needed

concerns.concern: Photon-energy independence cannot distinguish surface states from surface-bulk projected states, yet it is used to assign surface states.
concerns.quote: This test cannot separate SSs from SBPSs; only linewidth and disorder sensitivity remain.

concerns.concern: A single-photon-energy map is never strictly SBZ-periodic, so Fig. 1f does not demonstrate intrinsic non-commensurability.
concerns.quote: Such maps are *never* strictly SBZ-periodic, on (001) or any other facet.

concerns.concern: The periodicity extracted from the map in Fig. 1e should be determined quantitatively, for example by autocorrelation or FFT.
concerns.quote: the green-box periodicity "extracted from (e)" should be determined quantitatively, for example by autocorrelation or FFT of the map.

concerns.concern: The novelty of the disorder-based strategy and of the SBPS/SBRS terminology is overstated. Quenching surface states with disorder or adsorbates is well established, and the terms largely rename known concepts.
concerns.quote: The terms "SBPS" and "SBRS" largely rename projected bulk continua and surface resonances.

concerns.concern: The XPS shows chemically modified sites on the uneven surface, so the claim that the termination is unchanged should be softened or quantitatively supported.
concerns.quote: This suggests chemically modified sites, not merely structural disorder.

concerns.concern: Key Green's function methodological details are missing: the Wannier model and fit quality, the principal-layer definition for (103), and the broadening used.
concerns.quote: the tight-binding/Wannier model (projections, disentanglement windows, quality of the band fit); the principal-layer definition for (103); the broadening used.

concerns.concern: The 8 K measurements are close to T_N ≈ 7 K, and possible short-range order or fluctuation effects should be discussed.
concerns.quote: T_N of NdAlSi is ≈ 7 K, so the I05 data are close to the transition. Please comment on possible short-range order or fluctuation effects.

concerns.concern: "SOC included as a second-order perturbation" is unusual for VASP and needs clarification.
concerns.quote: The phrase "SOC included as a second-order perturbation" is unusual for VASP and should be clarified.

concerns.concern: The 6×6×6 k-mesh is coarse for a semimetal and needs justification.
concerns.quote: A 6×6×6 k-mesh is coarse for a semimetal and should be justified.

concerns.concern: The inner potential used for the k⊥ conversion and the k⊥ path for Fig. 3 should be stated.
concerns.quote: Please state the inner potential used for the hν → k⊥ conversion and show the k⊥ path for Fig. 3.

concerns.concern: The quoted photon-energy ranges are inconsistent between the text and the figure captions.
concerns.quote: 125–195 eV in the text, 125–205 eV in the Fig. 3b caption, and ~80–240 eV in Fig. 3e.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3 replica argument is not quantitative, since the boxed features are not identical. Denser sampling or an explicit computation of |G_normal| is needed.
concerns.quote: Denser sampling, or an explicit computation of the k⊥ period |G_normal|, would make the replica argument quantitative.

concerns.concern: ARPES–DFT agreement is asserted only qualitatively, and quantitative comparisons of band positions and Fermi-level offset are needed.
concerns.quote: quantitative comparisons (band positions, Fermi-level offset) would help.

concerns.concern: The supplementary claim that slab surface states agree better with experiment for (001) is supported only by self-citation.
concerns.quote: needs support beyond self-citation.

concerns.concern: The in-plane momentum axes should be defined relative to crystallographic directions, and the sample azimuth given.
concerns.quote: Define the in-plane axes (k_y, k∥) with respect to crystallographic directions, and give the sample azimuth.

concerns.concern: The surface terminations are described inconsistently between the Methods and SM Sec. 4.
concerns.quote: The terminations are described inconsistently

concerns.concern: NdAlSi is mislabelled as body-centred cubic instead of body-centred tetragonal.
concerns.quote: NdAlSi is body-centred *tetragonal*, not "body-centred cubic."

concerns.concern: The wrong reflection condition is given for I-centring; the all-even/all-odd rule belongs to F-centring.
concerns.quote: The reflection condition for I-centring is h+k+l = 2n. "All-even/all-odd" is the F-centring rule.

concerns.concern: "Curie temperature" should be replaced with the appropriate magnetic transition.
concerns.quote: "Curie temperature" should also be replaced with the appropriate transition.

concerns.concern: Refs. [48, 49] (DFPT, Quantum ESPRESSO) are cited but not used anywhere in the text.
concerns.quote: Refs. [48, 49] (DFPT, Quantum ESPRESSO) are cited but not used anywhere in the text.

concerns.concern: The SM reference cited for the lattice constants is a different paper from the one implied.
concerns.quote: SM ref. [3], cited for the lattice constants, is a different paper from the one implied.

concerns.concern: The language is frequently promotional and should be toned down.
concerns.quote: Language is frequently promotional, e.g. "universal criterion," "inaugurate a new frontier," "never explored," "remarkable accuracy."

concerns.concern: The phrase "Perhaps typically preserving the canonical picture" is an unclear hedge.
concerns.quote: "Perhaps typically preserving the canonical picture" (p. 7) is an unclear hedge.

concerns.concern: Typo: "BCC paradox" should read "BBC paradox".
concerns.quote: "BCC paradox" (p. 6) should read "BBC paradox."

concerns.concern: Ref. [21] misspells SrAl₄.
concerns.quote: Ref. [21] "SraAl4" should be SrAl₄.

concerns.concern: Ref. [29] has the wrong publication year.
